PURPOSE: We present the meshfree Discretization-Corrected Particle Strength Exchange (DC PSE) methodology for accurate wall shear stress (WSS) computation in patient-specific vascular geometries represented by unstructured point clouds. METHODS: The proposed framework reconstructs spatial derivatives directly on irregular node distributions. The methodology is validated using fully developed Poiseuille flow, for which analytical solutions for both velocity and WSS are available. The proposed scheme is applied to transient blood flow simulations in patient-specific arterial geometries reconstructed from medical imaging. Mesh refinement convergence studies were performed to verify the accuracy and numerical robustness of the proposed approach. Velocity fields were computed by solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations using the OpenFOAM finite-volume solver, while WSS was evaluated from the reconstructed wall velocity gradients using the proposed DC PSE formulation. Numerical predictions were compared with WSS obtained directly from OpenFOAM. RESULTS: The proposed methodology accurately reproduced the analytical WSS distribution for the benchmark problem, achieving a normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) of 1.2 × 10 - 4    , compared with 1.2 × 10 - 2    obtained with OpenFOAM post-processing tools using a reference finite-volume solution. The reconstructed velocity derivatives remained stable on irregular point distributions. In patient-specific blood flow simulations, the proposed framework produced smooth and physically consistent WSS distributions throughout the cardiac cycle, accurately resolving regions of elevated and low shear associated with vessel curvature and bifurcations. CONCLUSIONS: The DC PSE framework provides an accurate, robust, and computationally efficient approach for WSS estimation in image-based cardiovascular Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations. By improving the reconstruction of wall velocity gradients on complex geometries, the proposed methodology substantially enhances the accuracy of wall-derived hemodynamic metrics without requiring specialized boundary-layer meshes. The method offers a flexible post-processing framework that can be readily integrated into existing CFD pipelines and has significant potential for patient-specific cardiovascular modeling and computational medical physics applications.

articles.title: Revealing hidden vascular patterns: a modified CEUS LI-RADS framework for HCC using super-resolution ultrasound.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the incremental value of super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) microvascular imaging in optimizing the contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) liver imaging reporting and data system (LI-RADS) for the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) diagnosis. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled high-risk patients for HCC from January 2024 to April 2025. Each patient underwent B-mode US, color Doppler flow imaging (CDFI), micro-flow imaging (MFI), conventional CEUS, and SRUS microvascular imaging examinations. Based on the two additional vascular features (capsular vessels and chaotic vessels) displayed by SRUS microvascular imaging, three novel criteria were developed for modified CEUS LI-RADS (LR). The LR-4 or LR-M lesions were reclassified to LR-5 using the following three criteria: (I) the presence of capsular vessels; (II) the presence of chaotic vessels; (III) the presence of capsular vessels or chaotic vessels. The diagnostic performance of modified CEUS LI-RADS using three HCC criteria was evaluated and compared with that of the original CEUS LI-RADS. The reference standard was pathologic confirmation or composite criteria. RESULTS: Overall, 593 patients with 593 lesions were enrolled. The visualization rate of the capsular and chaotic vessel features by SRUS is higher than that of CDFI, MFI, and the arterial phase of CEUS (all P < 0.05). The inter-observer agreement was substantial for capsular vessels (kappa = 0.742) and chaotic vessels (kappa = 0.631). Compared with the original CEUS LI-RADS, three novel criteria for modified CEUS LI-RADS demonstrated higher sensitivity, accuracy, and area under the curve (AUC) (all P < 0.05). Particularly, criterion III achieved the best sensitivity (89.80%), accuracy (89.38%), and AUC (0.891), without a significant decrease in specificity (88.48%). CONCLUSIONS: SRUS microvascular imaging is able to reveal hidden vascular patterns in refining CEUS LI-RADS for HCC diagnosis.

articles.title: Cross-View Constrained Encoder and Cross-Modal Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion Network for Congenital Heart Disease Identification.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a common structural birth defect, and early screening is important for improving prognosis. Clinical cardiac ultrasound combines brightness-mode (B-mode) and color Doppler images from multiple standard views to assess cardiac morphology and hemodynamic abnormalities. Existing case-level models remain limited in modeling information exchange among standard views within each modality and cross-modal fusion between B-mode morphology and Doppler hemodynamics. The proposed Cross-View Constrained Encoder and Cross-Modal Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion Network (CVCE-CMSHFNet) addresses these limitations through two complementary components: a Multi-View Constrained Encoder (MVCE) and a Bidirectional Progressive Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion (BiPSHF) module. MVCE models relationships among the eight standard views within each modality. Sinkhorn-constrained transport and a parallel gated transformation update the view representations. Training-time Intra-Modal View Covariance Diversity Regularization (IVCDR) separately penalizes covariance similarity among B-mode view representations and among Doppler view representations. BiPSHF performs bidirectional cross-modal interaction at the view, view-group, and case levels. The view-group level organizes the eight standard views into four study-specific groups based on anatomical relationships and clinical assessment roles. CVCE-CMSHFNet aims to support clinical diagnosis by providing a case-level CHD probability for physician reference. Evaluation included 384 complete eight-view dual-modality cases from a 506-subject single-center echocardiography database. CVCE-CMSHFNet achieved 95.64% accuracy, 95.23% F1 score, 97.05% AUC, 94.44% sensitivity, and 96.67% specificity.

articles.title: Swin-DDM-Net: A Swin Transformer-Based Framework with Direction Difference Maps for Nuclear Instance Segmentation and Classification.
articles.abstract: Accurate nuclear instance segmentation and classification are fundamental prerequisites for quantitative digital pathology, but automated analysis remains difficult because nuclei vary substantially in shape, size, staining, density, and class-specific morphology. Swin-DDM-Net combines a hierarchical Swin Transformer encoder with three task-specific decoder branches for nuclear foreground prediction, horizontal-vertical distance regression, and pixel-level nuclear classification. The predicted distance maps are transformed into a Direction Difference Map (DDM), which captures local direction discontinuities at touching nuclear boundaries and refines marker-controlled watershed segmentation. Experiments on six public histopathology patch datasets, including CoNSeP, Kumar, CPM-15, CPM-17, TNBC, and CRCHisto, show competitive instance segmentation, patch-level cross-domain generalization, and nuclear classification performance relative to classical tools, convolutional baselines, HoVer-Net, CDNet, CellViT, and Mudslide under the evaluated settings. The results support the value of combining Transformer-based contextual representation with explicit instance geometry for cell-level computational pathology. The method should be interpreted as benchmark-level algorithmic evidence; statistical uncertainty analysis, dataset-license confirmation, public code and weight release, and external whole-slide-image (WSI) validation remain necessary before clinical deployment.

articles.title: PINet: A Pediatric Intussusception Network with Dual-Scale Guided Attention for Auxiliary Diagnosis Task Using Ultrasonography Images.
articles.abstract: Ultrasonography (USG) is the primary image modality for diagnosing pediatric intussusception, yet automated identification remains challenging due to severe bowel gas artifacts, acoustic reverberation, and edematous boundary blurring. Moreover, diagnostic uncertainty is exacerbated by the scarcity of large-scale clinical cohorts and ubiquitous acoustic speckle that frequently obscures critical pathognomonic landmarks. To address this gap, we propose Pediatric Intussusception Network (PINet) via a dual-scale guided attention to feature fusion trained on a large real-world pediatric intussusception dataset (RPID), which is used to predict anomalous classifications and improve lesion area learning. PINet integrates three complementary modules: (1) a position-attention module (PAM) to model concentric topological priors and suppress isolated gas artifacts; (2) a dual attention feature fusion (DAF) module combining strip pooling attention with dynamic alignment for multi-scale context aggregation; and (3) an informative context enhancement (ICE) module for low-contrast boundary refinement. It was trained on a largest reported dataset using 9871 USG images from 4026 patients. The result of PINet achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with 87.44% balanced accuracy and 98.09% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The clinical utility of the proposed PINet is demonstrated through robust performance across lesion sizes, accurate localization despite anatomical noise, and effective boundary delineation in low-contrast regions.

articles.title: Radiologist Workstation Configuration Preferences: Converging Evidence Toward Best Practices.
articles.abstract: Diagnostic radiologists spend much of their professional time interpreting imaging studies using a variety of workstation and monitor configurations. Despite well-established ergonomic principles, there are no widely accepted recommendations regarding monitor configuration, application placement, or peripheral device selection. This variability, particularly across academic medical centers with diverse workstation configurations, may contribute to musculoskeletal injury, workflow inefficiency, cognitive burden, and challenges integrating artificial intelligence (AI) applications. This study characterizes radiologist workstation configurations and determines whether similar usage patterns emerge across two independent national needs assessments. The findings from both assessments were compared. The first consisted of live audience polling during an RSNA 2025 educational session on radiologist ergonomics (n = 54). The second was an online survey distributed through professional LinkedIn and radiology social media communities (n = 49). Survey questions evaluated monitor number and orientation, workstation layout, application placement, ergonomic practices, sit-stand workstation use, and peripheral devices. Both assessments demonstrated similar workstation preferences. Most respondents in both the RSNA poll (n = 54) and online needs assessment (n = 49) used four-monitor equivalent configurations consisting of two portrait diagnostic monitors (often combined into one 30″ landscape) flanked by two supplemental monitors. Dictation was most commonly displayed on the left supplemental monitor, adjacent to the current examination (on the left diagnostic monitor). Respondents reported diverse placement of worklists, thumbnails, AI tools, peer review, electronic medical records, and advanced visualization applications. Sit-stand workstations were widely used, with most respondents standing 10-30% of the workday. Gaming mice with hyperscrolling functionality were the predominant pointing devices with very similar functions (window/level, measure, arrow, zoom/pan, and ROI). Two independent national needs assessments revealed consistent patterns in radiologist workstation configurations despite differences in survey methodology and participant populations. These findings suggest an emerging, flexible de facto standard that could guide ergonomic recommendations, workstation design and procurement, residency training, workflow optimization, and AI integration.

articles.title: Multicenter external validation of CT-based deep learning for proximal femoral fracture classification and quantitative fracture-line assessment.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and externally validate a CT-based deep learning CAD system for proximal femoral fracture classification and fracture-line angle quantification and to preliminarily evaluate its clinical utility in a reader study. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, coronal CT images from four institutions were used for training (259 patients, 19,844 annotated images) and internal validation (91 patients, 92 hips). External validation included 200 patients from independent institutions scanned with CT systems from two vendors. A ResNet-50-based convolutional neural network was used to perform fracture region segmentation, fracture classification, pelvic fracture detection, and fracture line angle estimation. The diagnostic performance and fracture-line angle agreement were evaluated using internal and external validation datasets. An exploratory reader study involving six readers was conducted to assess the effects of CAD assistance. RESULTS: Overall classification accuracy was 95.7% (κ = 0.944) internally and 91.5% (κ = 0.887) externally; F1-score ranges were 0.927-0.982 and 0.667-0.952, respectively. The fracture-line angle mean absolute errors were 4.54° and 6.26°, approaching the interobserver errors between orthopedic specialists (3.64° and 5.18°), with corresponding ICCs of 0.817 and 0.736, respectively. In the exploratory reader study, residents showed higher sensitivity with CAD assistance for non-displaced femoral neck fractures (0.78 vs. 0.47), with high specificity. CONCLUSION: This multicenter CT-based CAD system demonstrated accurate and generalizable fracture region segmentation, proximal femoral fracture classification, and objective fracture line angle quantification across independent datasets. The proposed approach has the potential to support diagnosis and preoperative assessment of proximal femoral fractures.

articles.title: Hepatic Ectopic Pregnancy: A 70-Year Systematic Review Focusing on Ultrasound Diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Hepatic ectopic pregnancy (HEP) represents a rare form of abdominal ectopic pregnancy. Its nonspecific clinical present9ation poses a diagnostic challenge, and delayed recognition may culminate in catastrophic intra-abdominal hemorrhage. Scattered case reports provide fragmented descriptions of clinical features, sonographic findings, and treatments. This review aims to provide an overview of HEP and the application of ultrasound in diagnosis and follow up of HEP based on 70 years of published literature.

articles.title: Whole-body fetal 3D CINE MRI with low flip angle balanced steady-state free precession acquisition within the specific absorption rate limit at 1.5 T.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a three-dimensional (3D) CINE magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequence for assessing whole-body fetal movements within the specific absorption rate (SAR) limit, and to evaluate its clinical feasibility. METHODS: A 3D balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) CINE MRI sequence was developed at 1.5 T within a whole-body averaged SAR of ≤ 2 W/kg. Half-scan artifacts (zero-valued pixels) and flip angle (FA) effects on signal intensity and contrast were assessed in phantoms. Seventeen fetal examinations (14 with the final protocol) were evaluated visually by two readers and by the contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) between fetal tissues and amniotic fluid. RESULTS: Zero-valued pixels appeared with the half-scan technique and increased as the half-scan factor decreased. The contrast between the phantoms was greater at higher FAs. Reducing the FA to 25° allowed a shorter TR within the SAR limit, enabling a 3D slab placed over the fetus to be acquired without the half-scan technique at a temporal resolution of approximately 320 msec (whole-body SAR, 1.59-1.94 W/kg). The CNRs between the amniotic fluid and the brain, lung, abdomen and limbs were 24.1 ± 10.6, 23.1 ± 12.8, 27.3 ± 14.3 and 30.9 ± 9.2, respectively. With the final protocol, both readers identified fetal movement in 11 of 14 examinations (κ = 1.00), and fold-over artifacts impaired the evaluation in two and three examinations, respectively. CONCLUSION: Low-FA 3D bSSFP CINE MRI at 1.5 T enables visualization of whole-body fetal movements within the SAR limit at a temporal resolution of approximately 320 msec.

articles.title: Slice orientation impacts phase values in susceptibility weighted imaging of the deep gray matter in patients with multiple sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Phase quantification has emerged as a critical method for monitoring disease progression and evaluating treatment efficacy in Multiple Sclerosis (MS) due to its high sensitivity to pathological iron deposition and microstructural changes. Despite its utility, most researchers continue to prioritize anatomical alignment protocols such as orientation parallel to the anterior-posterior commissure AC-PC line, which often result in slice angulations that deviate significantly, sometimes reaching 20ο, from the main magnetic field (B0). This prospective study evaluated the impact of such orientation variations on Susceptibility-Weighted Angiography (SWAN) phase values in twenty-six MS patients using a 1.5 T scanner. Each subject underwent two SWAN acquisitions: a standardized zero-alignment to B0 and a conventional anatomical alignment. Quantitative ROI analysis across seven bilateral deep gray matter structures revealed that phase magnitudes were consistently and significantly higher under zero alignment compared to anatomical alignment (p < 0.05). Furthermore, a progressive reduction in phase magnitude was observed as the angular deviation from B0 increased, confirming a clear inverse relationship between acquisition obliquity and susceptibility sensitivity. These findings suggest that current anatomical alignment practices may sub-optimize the detection of susceptibility-related biomarkers. Consequently, standardizing acquisitions to zero alignment is essential for ensuring the reproducibility of phase quantification and enhancing its clinical value for monitoring disease and therapeutic outcomes in MS.

articles.title: Spontaneous paraduodenal hematomas: An observational study of risk factors, natural history, and outcomes.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Assess risk factors, complications, and treatment strategies for spontaneous paraduodenal hematomas. METHODS: Our institutional radiology database was used to retrospectively identify paraduodenal hematomas from reports dated 2000-2025. Two fellowship-trained abdominal radiologists independently reviewed images for paraduodenal hematoma. Studies were excluded if the hematoma was not primarily involving the duodenum, or if there was antecedent regional trauma or recent surgery/instrumentation. The electronic health record was reviewed for risk factors of paraduodenal hematoma (e.g., pancreatitis, gastric/duodenal ulcer, vasculitis, antiplatelet/anticoagulant use). Follow-up CT and MR reports were also reviewed for hematoma resolution or complications. Interventions were recorded. RESULTS: A total of 214 reports were identified. After inclusion/exclusion criteria, the final cohort included 18 patients. Pancreatitis was present in 4/18 patients (22%). Duodenal ulcer disease was documented in 3/18 (17%). Two patients had underlying vascular disease. 12/18 (67%) patients were on anticoagulant and/or antiplatelet therapy at the time of paraduodenal hematoma diagnosis. Complications occurred in 7/18 patients (39%), including gastric outlet obstruction (3/18, 17%), small bowel obstruction (1/18, 6%), biliary obstruction (1/18, 6%), pancreatitis (1/18, 6%), and superinfection (1/18, 6%). Two (11%) patients died. Interventions included catheter angiography in 11/18 patients (61%), with embolization performed in 9/18 (50%). Other interventions included surgical drainage (1/18, 6%) and percutaneous aspiration (1/18, 6%). CONCLUSION: Spontaneous paraduodenal hematomas are rare. Many affected patients are on antithrombotic agents, and some patients have duodenal ulcer, pancreatitis, or vascular disease. Catheter angiography/embolization tend to be performed to control bleeding. Complications are primarily related to obstruction of adjacent structures.

articles.title: Simulated teams in radiology: A simple innovation to enhance belongingness and learning.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Belongingness has been shown to reduce burnout, with team engagement shown to enhance a sense of belonging. Diagnostic radiology trainees often work independently from their peers and in the post-pandemic era radiology trainees may be at different sites than their faculty with limited-contact, remote read-outs. OBJECTIVE: We created a month-long simulated team near-peer mentorship pilot program on our general Nuclear Medicine service. We hypothesized this program would enhance trainees' sense of belongingness without hindering learning on service. METHODS: Radiology fellows and R1s spent 15 min reviewing a daily case, modeled after the mentorship structure of residents on "rounds" in surgical and medical specialties. Multi-method programmatic evaluation included a voluntary, anonymous survey about belongingness sent to all radiology residents and NM fellows in our institution as well as focus groups of pilot program participants. RESULTS: From November 2023 to April 2024, 9 R1s and 5 fellows participated in the pilot. Program participants reported higher Likert-scale ratings of statements assessing belongingness such as "I feel like a part of a community on service." In the focus groups, two major themes explained the trainees' sense of increased belonging: the simulated team program 1) encouraged additional interactions throughout the day and 2) enhanced psychological safety on service. CONCLUSION: In this hypothesis-generating pilot study, a near-peer mentorship program simulating a team of diagnostic radiology R1s and fellows seemed to enhance perceived sense of belonging and learning on service. Small, time-efficient educational initiatives may have big impacts on our trainees.
